subject: Telemetry log retention & header redaction — follow-up
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <p.rao@medivue.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry log retention & header redaction — follow-up

Hi Priyanka — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the pilot appropriately:

- Goal: Medivue wants request/response logging for troubleshooting but cannot retain or surface PII in logs. You mentioned special concern about Authorization headers and trace IDs that tie back to patient records.
- What we heard: retain minimal metadata for 30 days for product-level debugging, and an anonymized audit stream for 1 year accessible to security.

Questions for you:
1) Are trace IDs considered identifiers in your compliance model (i.e., would hashing still be considered pseudonymous), or do they need to be removed entirely?
2) For request/response payloads, do you want full payload redaction, field-level masking, or a policy where only non-sensitive fields are logged?
3) Can you share one or two sample log lines (sanitized) so our engineers can validate transformation rules?

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll provide two technical options for pilot: (A) salted-hash pseudonymization for trace IDs (reversible only to your tenant with customer salt), and (B) full-strip (remove trace IDs entirely). We’ll include config toggles and observability tradeoffs.
- Send over sample log lines and any internal documentation on what you classify as PII.
- Schedule a 30-minute security/deep-dive with our infra engineer (Sean) and your security lead next week.

Attached: redaction-checklist.pdf (checklist template we use for pilots).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[t] +1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: redaction-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyanka Rao <p.rao@medivue.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@medivue.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry log retention & header redaction — follow-up

Thanks, Tessa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Trace IDs: our privacy team treats any identifier that can be correlated back to a patient session as personal data. Hashing is acceptable only if it is provably non-reversible without the customer salt and you sign an attestation that you do not keep the salt.
- Headers: Authorization and X-Patient-ID must be removed from any log retained outside our VPC. Other headers (User-Agent, Accept) are OK.
- Payloads: we prefer field-level redaction for free-text fields (regex-based scrub) and full strip for any base64 blobs or attachments.
- Retention: 30 days for full, human-readable logs; 365 days for aggregated/anonymized audit stream (no request/response payloads).

I’ve attached our initial redaction spec and a couple of sanitized log examples — hope these help. We’d like to include infrastructure security (Arjun) on the follow-up. Can Sean and your security engineer join?

Priyanka
Priyanka Rao
Head of Cloud Security, Medivue Health
[p] +1 617-555-0194
[Attachment: redaction-specs.docx (docx)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Telemetry log retention & header redaction — follow-up

Tessa / Monica — quick internal note after Priyanka’s response. Key risks and suggested approach:

- Hashing vs stripping tradeoff: salted-hash (SHA256 with tenant salt stored in HSM) satisfies pseudonymization if we do not keep salt. But operations impact: we lose cross-request tracing unless Medivue provides the salt during debug sessions. Full-strip preserves privacy but reduces our ability to do end-to-end request correlation during early pilot.
- Headers: we can add a header-filtering pipeline stage that drops Authorization/X-Patient-ID at ingest for hosted endpoints, and enforce retention policies per tenant config.
- Payloads: we can implement regex-based scrubbers (configurable) and a hard rule to drop binary blobs. We should capture a short sample transformation report for each pilot run.

Proposed pilot deliverables:
1) Two-mode ingest pipeline: pseudonymize (salted-hash) OR strip for trace IDs (customer-selected).
2) Header filter for Authorization and X-Patient-ID applied before logs leave customer tenant.
3) Retention config: 30 days full logs; 365 days aggregated audit stream (no payloads).
4) A short SOW and pilot success criteria doc.

Ask: Tessa, can you confirm whether Medivue requires that we do not persist the salt anywhere? If so we offer a model where the salt is customer-managed in their KMS and Redwood receives ephemeral proofs only. I’ll draft the pilot-plan.pdf and a short security note.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-plan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <p.rao@medivue.com>
Cc: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@medivue.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry log retention & header redaction — follow-up

Priyanka — thanks for the spec and the examples, that was very helpful. Here’s what Redwood can commit to for the pilot and immediate next steps:

- Pilot config: salted-SHA256 pseudonymization for trace IDs with customer-managed salt in your KMS (Redwood will not store the salt). We’ll provide a verification attestation. Option to switch to full-strip for production if you prefer.
- Header handling: Authorization and X-Patient-ID will be removed at ingest for hosted endpoints. For Private/VPC deployments we will provide deploy-time filters and docs for your infra team to enforce the same.
- Payloads & retention: apply field-level regex scrubbers for free-text, drop binary blobs. Full logs retained for 30 days; anonymized audit stream (no request/response payloads) retained for 365 days.

Action items:
- Priyanka/Arjun: please confirm you can provide sample logs via the Drive link and the name/email of your legal/compliance reviewer for an attestation (cc them on the next thread).
- Redwood: Sean will share pilot-plan.pdf and a short security attestation. I’ll open a HubSpot deal record and attach the SOW.
- Schedule: propose 30-minute pilot kickoff on Wed June 5 at 10am ET — are you available?

Links: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/MDV-4832 ; Sample logs upload: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-sample-log-lines

Best,
Tessa
